description: Recorded-audio wake-word evaluation corpus for SaySo satellite
wake_rule: The phrase /seɪ soʊ/ wakes only in isolation: any word in front of it disqualifies the wake, a word after it does not. Both realizations ('SaySo' and 'say so') are wakes. See docs/WAKE_WORD_DATA.md.

categories.positive_sayso: Isolated fused SaySo wake, nothing spoken in front of it
categories.positive_say_so_two_word: Isolated two-word 'say so' wake; a different acoustic event from the fused token, so it is scored separately
categories.continuous_command: SaySo followed by a command in one breath (e.g. SaySo turn off the kitchen)
categories.negative_say_so_carrier: The phrase said after another word, so not a wake under the isolation rule
categories.negative_tv_conversation: TV or conversation background without an intentional wake
categories.negative_distance_noise: Distance chatter or background noise with no wake phrase

cases.notes: Fused realization, close mic. The baseline positive.

PENDING CAPTURE: fused realization at 1.5-3 m. Production audio sits ~22 dB below the TTS positives, so distance decides recall, but no reviewed capture exists yet and a case nobody can populate is not coverage.
Two-word realization, isolated, nothing in front of it. Scored apart from the fused token because neither realization can stand in for the other.
A word after the phrase does not disqualify the wake. This case is the positive half of the isolation rule.
"if you say so". The phrase is preceded by two words, so it is not a wake. The same event in clean TTS scores 0.141 today, which is coincidence rather than the rule.
One word, then the phrase, then a command: "and say so turn off the kitchen". The hard case -- everything after the leading word looks exactly like a real continuous command.
Background speech with no wake phrase at all.
Distance chatter and room noise, no wake phrase. A SaySo at distance belongs in positive_sayso (pos_sayso_distance), not here.
